home.intro: Reach your Kubernetes clusters safely. Select a cluster to get started.

empty.title: No cluster available
empty.description: You do not have access to any Kubernetes cluster yet. Ask your administrator for the permissions you need.

landing.tagline: Your secure gateway to Kubernetes: centralise and secure access to your Kubernetes APIs, one place for every cluster.

security.title: Stronger security
security.text: Centralised authentication, with permissions you can narrow for every Kubernetes cluster.

unified.title: One interface
unified.text: One place to reach all your clusters, instead of juggling tools and logins. It can also plug into other portals.

instant.title: Instant access
instant.text: Automatic redirection to the APIs with SSO. No impersonation: access stays scoped and partitioned.

teams.title: Team management
teams.text: Control who reaches what, per user and per cluster, with RBAC delegation.

audit.title: Audit
audit.text: Follow access as it happens and audit how your Kubernetes resources are used.

flexible.title: Flexible configuration
flexible.text: Fit ProxyAuthK8S to your infrastructure, with several identity providers and configurations.

login.title: Log in
login.text: Sign in to ProxyAuthK8S, which lists the clusters your permissions give you.

explore.title: Explore your clusters
explore.text: See the Kubernetes APIs you can reach and whether they support SSO.

access.title: Connect in one step
access.text: Pick a cluster: the proxy sends you to that cluster's own SSO.

use.title: Talk to the Kubernetes API
use.text: Use kubectl, k9s or any other Kubernetes client.

landing.more: Documentation, the kubectl plugin and the source code:

about.title: About
about.lead: ProxyAuthK8S is an authenticating reverse proxy for Kubernetes: it puts your clusters behind your OIDC provider and applies your authorisation rules to every request.

entry.title: One entry point
entry.text: Every cluster sits behind ProxyAuthK8S: one URL, one identity provider.

oidc.title: OIDC authentication
oidc.text: Sign in through your IdP; tokens are validated (userinfo, audience, introspection) before any call reaches the cluster.

authz.title: Fine-grained authorisation
authz.text: Groups allowed per cluster, filtered resources, namespaces, ports and verbs, quotas, bans and an audit trail.

kubectl.title: Native kubectl
kubectl.text: The kubectl proxyauth plugin handles login, the keyring and the kubeconfig for you.

architecture.label: Architecture
architecture.text: How the proxy, the IdP and the clusters fit together

api.label: API reference
api.text: The interactive API of this server

clusterCallback.title: Cluster login
clusterCallback.description: Finishing the login to the cluster {cluster} in the namespace {ns}.
clusterCallback.waiting: Fetching your tokens from the identity provider…
clusterCallback.failedText: The authentication tokens could not be retrieved. Try again or contact your administrator.
clusterCallback.failedToast: The authentication could not be completed.

noSso.title: Cluster without SSO
noSso.description: Configuration for the cluster {cluster} in the namespace {ns}.
noSso.explanation: This cluster does not use SSO/OIDC. It is reached through the proxy with your current token, and the generated kubeconfig points every request at the proxy.
noSso.kubeconfigText: This kubeconfig uses the proxy as its endpoint and your token, valid while your ProxyAuth session is.
noSso.notFoundText: The requested cluster cannot be found or reached. Check the URL or contact your administrator.
noSso.missingParams: Parameters are missing from the URL.
noSso.usesSso: This cluster uses SSO, taking you back home…

exchange.title: Cluster in token exchange
exchange.description: Configuration for the cluster {cluster} in the namespace {ns}.
exchange.explanation: This cluster takes your ProxyAuth session: the proxy exchanges it with the cluster's identity provider, so there is no login to the cluster and no cluster token on your machine.
exchange.kubeconfigText: This kubeconfig asks the kubectl plugin for your session. Once, first: kubectl proxyauth login --server-url <proxy URL>, then kubectl proxyauth -n {ns} login {cluster} (no browser for this cluster).

kubeconfig.title: Kubernetes configuration
kubeconfig.standardText: A kubeconfig with a static token: use it to connect directly with the token you received.
kubeconfig.pluginText: A kubeconfig for the kubectl-proxyauth plugin, which manages and refreshes the tokens.
kubeconfig.cliText: Connect from the command line with the kubectl-proxyauth plugin, the recommended way with kubectl.
